access.fees: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful Pass required for parking at the Upper Dungeness Trailhead (USFS); once inside Olympic National Park, a wilderness camping permit (with its own fee) is required for overnight stays.
access.notes: No separate climbing cost-recovery fee like Mount Rainier’s $82 — only the standard entrance fee and wilderness camping permit apply.
access.rules: NPS wilderness permit required; bear canisters are mandatory for food/scented items in Royal Basin; camp only in designated sites (Royal Creek, Lower Royal Meadow, or Royal Lake); no campfires above 3,500 ft; follow Leave No Trace practices throughout.
access.permit: Royal Basin is a quota/reservation area in Olympic National Park - permits for the May 15-October 15 season are released around April 15 via recreation.gov (10:00 AM EDT / 7:00 AM PDT); contact the Olympic Wilderness Information Center (360-565-3100) for current availability.
access.landManager: Mixed jurisdiction: Olympic National Forest (Buckhorn Wilderness) for the trailhead and lower approach trail, transitioning to Olympic National Park at the park boundary near Royal Basin.
access.land_manager: Mixed jurisdiction: Olympic National Forest (Buckhorn Wilderness) for the trailhead and lower approach trail, transitioning to Olympic National Park at the park boundary near Royal Basin.
access.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass, Interagency Pass or Scan & Pay at the Upper Dungeness Trailhead — $5 per vehicle per day or $30 annual. The trailhead is on Olympic National Forest land (Quilcene Ranger District), so no Olympic National Park entrance fee is charged to park there.
access.passRequired: Northwest Forest Pass (or America the Beautiful Pass) at the Upper Dungeness Trailhead; NPS wilderness permit required once inside Olympic National Park.

overnight_permit.what: Olympic National Park wilderness permit — quota at Royal Lake, not free
overnight_permit.where: Reserve on Recreation.gov; the Royal Lake quota sells out quickly. Bear canisters are required in Royal Basin.
